Reference / net/udp

net/udp#

Immutable observation of one received packet: sender, retained payload and explicit truncation flag.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let packet=Datagram(IpEndpoint(IpAddress("192.0.2.7"),5353),
    [byte(0),byte(255)],false);
packet.source().string(); // "192.0.2.7:5353"
packet.bytes();           // exact retained octets

Description#

Immutable observation of one received packet: sender, retained payload and explicit truncation flag. No socket I/O, decoding or inferred truncation. Empty payloads are packets, not EOF; even an empty retained prefix may be marked truncated. Discarded bytes and original packet size are not recoverable.

ByteSource exposes only this finite payload for explicit forwarding. It does not make a Datagram a byte stream or transfer sender metadata to a new send. Repeated observations preserve the snapshot; equality includes all metadata.

object UdpOptions#

object UdpOptions

Immutable UDP binding requests. Defaults disable address reuse, broadcast and dual stack. The flags are independent; constructor validation does not probe platforms or infer an address family. A future binding applies requests before bind and reports unsupported combinations for its selected family.

UdpOptions(address_reuse:true,broadcast:false,dual_stack:false);

Observations preserve exact flags; no socket option is changed by this value.

object UdpBinding#

object UdpBinding

Lazy UDP bind request. Construction retains only values; each socket() call creates a fresh Future, and repeated await of that Future shares one socket. Options are applied before bind; port zero is replaced by the OS-selected port. Failures close unpublished descriptors and are attributed to binding.

let socket=await UdpBinding(IpEndpoint(IpAddress("127.0.0.1"),0),
    UdpOptions()).socket();
socket.local_endpoint(); // actual bound address and OS-selected port
socket.close();          // also runs automatically on owner scope exit

role UdpMembership#

role UdpMembership

Owner of one bound nonblocking socket. datagram(limit) lazily receives one packet, retaining a bounded prefix and explicit truncation. Empty is not EOF. Each Future consumes once; repeat awaits observe the same captured packet. Non-positive limits fail before I/O. One receive may wait at a time; overlap reports NetworkFailure with kind resource_exhausted. Cancel removes readiness without consuming a later packet. Close wakes pending receives with NetworkClosed. The native receive buffer is 65536 bytes; IPv6 jumbograms are excluded. send(target,source) samples the ByteSource once on first await and submits one complete packet. Its int result counts bytes accepted by the OS (zero for an empty packet), not remote delivery. Repeated awaits never resend. Port zero and closed state fail before source evaluation; size failures retain the byte count in DatagramTooLarge. One send may wait independently of one receive. All aliases share closed state. Endpoint is a snapshot usable after close. The SocketState constructor is provider infrastructure; use UdpBinding. Lifecycle of an acquired membership, following fs/file.FileLocking. The socket executes acquisition and retains its private native state.

object UdpConnecting#

object UdpConnecting

Immutable request for a NEW socket with a fixed numeric peer. Construction and unstarted Futures do no I/O; each started connection() call owns a fresh bind/connect, while repeated await of the same Future shares its owner. This does not consume or mutate an existing public UdpSocket.

let request=UdpConnecting(IpEndpoint(IpAddress("127.0.0.1"),0),
    peer,UdpOptions());
let connection=await request.connection();

The unpublished UdpSocket is a scoped ownership anchor during native await. Returned UdpConnection retains it; failure/cancellation releases it. Binding failures and connecting failures retain their respective operation categories.

object UdpConnection#

object UdpConnection

Owner of one connected UDP socket. Only its fixed peer can send packets to datagram(limit); send(source) never accepts an alternate destination. Empty payload is a packet, not EOF; datagram preserves truncation explicitly. Endpoints are actual post-connect OS observations and survive closure. The native-state/owner constructor is infrastructure: use UdpConnecting.

Errors#

enum DatagramTooLarge#

enum DatagramTooLarge is Error = (size(size is int))

Failed UDP payload size, measured in bytes. The sending operation determines its effective limit; this immutable diagnostic only retains a non-negative attempted count. It holds no payload or socket and remains usable after close.

throw DatagramTooLarge.size(65508);
catch DatagramTooLarge.size(size) { ... } // 65508
